I have 4 kids, and I notice immediately when one of the kids is not where they are supposed to be. For instance, my youngest is one, but she makes her presence known. Whereas, my oldest is 10 and makes her presence known in a completely different way. My 2 year old is the loudest and bounciest of them all. I know when he's not around, especially because 2-3 yr olds are prone to trying to "run" and testing the rules.

Missing one of the kids, is very noticeable in our family (and for most large families). I'm sure my other kids wouldn't allow me to "leave one in the car". I don't even get to start the car/leave a place/go somewhere before I triple check to make sure that all the kids are where they are supposed to be. If you have that many kids, you have to do a head count, and have to make sure you are keeping an eye on all kids at all times. As their parent, it's your job to make sure that all of your kids are safe and that includes keeping an eye on them all before indulging in whatever the fuck I want to do (including attending church service).

How do you just forget that you have five kids that all go to bible study. Three years in, and this should be routine by now. With that many kids...you always have one trying to run the fuck away from you, one trying to go talk to their friends, one trying to do this/that, and so you are even more vigilant about where your kids are. (My kids swear I have eyes in the back of my head, and I think I just might have developed a super awesome "parent sensor" for them.)

Oh...and I saw the shitty comments that people wrote about how the older kids were responsible for the younger ones. At the end of the day, my oldest might help change a fucking diaper...but she sure as fuck is not 100% responsible for her siblings. That falls down to the parents, and they failed doing a head count or you know...being a fucking parent.

This article says all of the kids were supposed to be in the same bible class together. Even the 3 yr old. So, what, they all ran roughshod into bible class (most likely unattended) and the bible teacher didn't even ask where the 5th kid was? Or did the siblings cover for the parents? If the parents didn't let their kids run free reign, and physically took them to class, how did they not check to make sure all of them were inside...and only noticed AFTER the class was over? This whole story stinks.

Add on, most parents know that if you attempt to leave a 2-3 yr old anywhere...they have a massive fit. I dare to shut the bathroom door while going to the bathroom, and my son is on the other side trying to break down the door.

We're also not taking into account that that kidlet was sitting in an upright car seat, that while most 2-3 yr olds know how to unlock...parents have been "trained" to help that kidlet out of the car. Most cars are too high up off of the ground for a little kid to get out without assistance. That's why parents always reach towards the back of the car first, and make sure their little one is on the ground safely...and these parents have a van in pictures, so you know that little guy needed help getting out.

I am wondering if they had shown favoritism towards the siblings, and they left the "bad child" in the car as punishment. I've heard of things like this happening before (on the sensational news), and it's extremely fucked up logic. It boggles my mind that they would remember that the 4 older kids need to go to bible class (or just sent them to class), and not a one of those 6 people (4 kids, 2 adults) remembered the baby!

So...1) no head count, 2) most likely letting their kids run wild/free without keeping an eye on them, 3) didn't help their kid out of the car, 4) somehow ignored their kids' panic attack, 5) all kids attended the bible class and not even the bible class teachers/4 other siblings noticed the kid wasn't there?, etc...the list of failures just goes on and on.

I don't believe this story, and if it really was an accident...these people should not be parents to that many kids.
